title: Semver precedence compare and max_version
prompt:
The file semver.py in the repo root has two unimplemented functions: compare(a, b) and max_version(versions). Implement both according to Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 precedence, as specified below. Python 3.11, standard library only. Keep the module name semver.py and the two function names and signatures.

Run the visible tests from the repo root with: python3 -m unittest -v test_semver
They are only a partial sample of the required behaviour. More cases, including edge cases that follow from this spec, are checked later, so follow the spec exactly.

VERSION GRAMMAR: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]
- MAJOR, MINOR, PATCH are non-negative decimal integers written with the ASCII digits 0-9. No leading zeros (the single digit "0" is fine). They can be arbitrarily large; do not assume they fit in 64 bits.
- PRERELEASE (optional, starts at the first "-" after the core) is one or more dot-separated identifiers. An identifier is non-empty and made of [0-9A-Za-z-]. An identifier made only of digits is "numeric" and must not have leading zeros ("0" itself is fine). An identifier containing a letter or a hyphen is "alphanumeric": "0a", "01a" and "-" are alphanumeric, hence valid.
- BUILD (optional, starts at the first "+") is one or more dot-separated non-empty identifiers of [0-9A-Za-z-]. Leading zeros are allowed there.
- Anything else is invalid: a leading "v", leading or trailing whitespace (a trailing newline included), a missing component ("1.2"), an extra component ("1.2.3.4"), an empty prerelease or build ("1.2.3-", "1.2.3+"), an empty identifier ("1.2.3-a..b"), non-ASCII digits or letters, and any value that is not a str.

PRECEDENCE: compare by the first difference found, left to right.
1. MAJOR, then MINOR, then PATCH, each numerically.
2. If those are equal, a version WITH a prerelease has LOWER precedence than the same version without one.
3. If both have a prerelease, compare its identifiers left to right:
   - numeric vs numeric: as integers;
   - alphanumeric vs alphanumeric: in ASCII order (so "-" < digits < uppercase < lowercase, e.g. "Beta" < "alpha");
   - a numeric identifier is always LOWER than an alphanumeric one;
   - if all shared identifiers are equal, the version with fewer identifiers is lower.
4. BUILD metadata is IGNORED: "1.0.0+a" and "1.0.0+b" have equal precedence.

FUNCTIONS
- compare(a, b) returns exactly one of the ints -1, 0, 1 when a has lower, equal or higher precedence than b.
- max_version(versions) takes any iterable of version strings (consume it only once) and returns the ORIGINAL string (not a normalised one) of the highest-precedence entry. When several entries share the highest precedence (they differ only in build metadata) it returns the first of them. Every entry is validated: an invalid entry raises ValueError wherever it sits, even when it is the only entry. An empty iterable raises ValueError.

ERRORS: invalid input raises ValueError whose message contains repr() of the offending value. compare() validates BOTH arguments before comparing anything (a is checked first, then b), even when the answer would be obvious, for example when a == b or when the majors differ. When both are invalid, the error is about a.
